findings.finding: replyIfWarranted() posts the reply and persists the watermark in two independent try/catch blocks. If restClient.createPost() fails (caught, logged, swallowed), the second try/catch still unconditionally runs stateStore.writeLastSeenMs(post.createAt), advancing the persisted watermark past the message whose reply never went out. On the next catch-up (reconnect or restart), getPostsSince(dmChannelId, lastSeenMs + 1) will no longer include that post, so the operator's message is permanently dropped with no reply and no retry -- only the one error log line at the moment of failure. This is exactly the 'swallowed failure that silently loses data' pattern KAN-2 was created to eliminate (the ticket cites a bash script that 'swallowed curl failures' as the precedent failure mode), and it fires on the primary path on any transient Mattermost failure (500, timeout, rate limit), not just an edge case.
findings.evidence: src/daemon.ts:53-63 -- the writeLastSeenMs call is not inside the createPost try block and has no guard on whether createPost succeeded. The only test covering this path, daemon.test.ts 'logs loudly and does not throw when posting the reply fails' (lines 300-319), asserts logger.error was called but never asserts stateStore.writeLastSeenMs was NOT called, so the test suite does not catch the bug.
findings.expected: Only advance/persist the watermark after a successful createPost (or track failed posts separately for retry), so a transient post failure causes the message to be retried on next catch-up instead of silently vanishing.
findings.note: daemon.ts replyIfWarranted() now returns immediately (before touching the watermark) if createPost throws. stateStore.writeLastSeen() only runs after a successful createPost. Added a dedicated test 'logs loudly, does not throw, and does NOT advance the watermark when posting the reply fails' asserting stateStore.writeLastSeen was not called.

findings.finding: catchUp() fetches missed posts via getPostsSince(dmChannelId, lastSeenMs + 1). The '+1' assumes no other post can share the exact same create_at millisecond as the last-processed post. If a post the daemon already handled live (via WS) and a second post the operator sent in the same millisecond (e.g. a batch of quick messages, or a mobile client flushing a queue on reconnect) share that same create_at, the second post's timestamp is <= the persisted watermark and is silently excluded from the catch-up fetch -- it is never replied to and there is no log indicating anything was skipped.
findings.evidence: src/daemon.ts:78-90 and src/mattermostRestClient.ts:86-101 (getPostsSince passes sinceMs straight through as the 'since' query param). No test exercises two posts with equal createAt values across a reconnect.
findings.expected: Track the last-seen post id (not just its timestamp) and dedupe by id after fetching with an inclusive 'since', or otherwise make the boundary condition inclusive-safe for same-millisecond posts.
findings.note: stateStore now persists {lastSeenMs, lastSeenId} (LastSeen.id) instead of only a timestamp; catchUp() fetches inclusively with getPostsSince(dmChannelId, lastSeen.ms) and dedupes the already-processed post by id (fetched.filter(p => p.id !== lastSeen.id)) rather than relying on a +1 timestamp boundary. Old state files without an id fall back to the original exclusive ms+1 boundary for one catch-up (a real state file with no id exists on this host at ~/.local/state/control-plane-daemon/state.json, so the fallback matters for a live upgrade, not just theory). Test added for the same-millisecond dedupe case and for the legacy fallback.

findings.finding: getPostsSince() issues a single unpaginated GET to /api/v4/channels/:channelId/posts?since=. Mattermost's posts-since endpoint returns at most one page (server-default page size) per call; there is no page/per_page loop and no check for whether the result was truncated. If the daemon is offline long enough (or a crash-loop persists) that more messages accumulate in the DM than fit in one page, catch-up silently processes only the first page and the rest are never fetched, replied to, or logged as missing.
findings.evidence: src/mattermostRestClient.ts:86-101 -- single request, no pagination parameters or loop; src/daemon.ts:87 logs only the count actually returned, with no way to detect truncation.
findings.expected: Loop with page/per_page (or equivalent) until a short page is returned, or otherwise verify the fetched batch is complete before advancing the watermark, and log if the API indicates more data is available.
findings.note: Confirmed via Mattermost's API reference that `since` cannot be combined with page/per_page/before/after and is capped at 1000 posts per call. getPostsSince() now loops: whenever a page comes back at exactly the 1000-post cap, it re-issues with since = (newest createAt in that page) + 1 and accumulates, only stopping once a short page returns -- so a long outage no longer silently truncates at page one. Also logs a warn line ('...page cap... fetching the next page') each time this happens, so truncation risk is visible even before the loop's coverage is trusted. Added tests for both the multi-page (1001 posts) and single-short-page cases.

findings.finding: The chezmoi re-run hash manifest lists the systemd unit, package.json, and every src/*.ts file, but omits package-lock.json. Because chezmoi only re-runs this script (and therefore only re-runs npm install / systemctl restart) when the rendered content of a listed file changes, bumping a dependency version in package-lock.json (e.g. a security patch pulled in without touching package.json) will not trigger a reinstall or restart -- the running daemon silently keeps using the old dependency tree. This directly violates the design principle stated in the script's own comment immediately above the manifest ('Forgetting to list a file here means editing it would silently NOT redeploy -- exactly the kind of quiet failure KAN-2 exists to avoid').
findings.evidence: run_onchange_install-control-plane-daemon.sh.tmpl:11-29 -- the comment describes the invariant; the manifest below it (lines 17-29) does not include package-lock.json even though `npm install --omit=dev` (line ~50 of the same script) reads it to pin installed versions.
findings.expected: Add package-lock.json to the sha256sum manifest alongside package.json.
findings.note: Added a `lockfile:` line hashing dot_local/share/control-plane-daemon/package-lock.json to the re-run manifest in run_onchange_install-control-plane-daemon.sh.tmpl, alongside package.json, so a lockfile-only dependency bump now changes the script's rendered content and triggers reinstall + restart.

findings.finding: mkdir -p "$env_dir" runs before umask 077 is set, so ~/.config/control-plane-daemon is created under the caller's default umask (commonly 022, i.e. world-readable/listable) rather than restricted. The token file itself is still written under umask 077 and additionally chmod 600'd, so the secret value is not exposed -- only the directory's existence/listing is slightly less restricted than it could be, and the path is already derivable from the world-readable systemd unit file's EnvironmentFile= line, so the practical exposure is negligible.
findings.expected: Set umask 077 before the mkdir -p, or chmod 700 the directory explicitly after creating it.
findings.note: Swapped the order in run_onchange_install-control-plane-daemon.sh.tmpl: `umask 077` now runs before `mkdir -p "$env_dir"`, so the directory itself is created 0700 instead of under the caller's default umask. No file creation happens later in the script, so leaving umask 077 in effect for the rest of the script is safe.

findings.finding: replyIfWarranted() logs on failure (logger.error) but never logs on success -- there is no info-level confirmation that a reply was actually posted. Combined with F1, this means the only journald evidence that the operator's message was ever answered is its absence of an error line, which is not a positive, independently-verifiable signal of delivery.
findings.evidence: src/daemon.ts:53-64 -- no logger.info/debug call after a successful restClient.createPost().
findings.expected: Add an info-level log line (e.g. postId, dmChannelId) after a successful reply, so delivery is directly observable in journald rather than inferred from the absence of an error.
findings.note: Added logger.info('posted reply to Mattermost', { postId, channelId }) in daemon.ts replyIfWarranted() right after a successful createPost. Added a test asserting this exact info log is emitted with the post id and dm channel id.
